prompt: An exchange proof for earliest-finish-first uses a greedy meeting g and an optimal schedule O whose first meeting o differs from g. Which statement justifies replacing o with g while preserving validity and the number of meetings?

options.text: Since g is shorter than o, g fits wherever o did
options.explanation: Earliest finish doesn't mean shortest: g might be longer than o and start earlier. The proof relies on *end* times, not lengths.

options.text: g ends no later than o, and all other meetings in O start at or after o ends
options.explanation: Correct. g ends no later than o, so anything that was compatible with o (by starting after o ended) is also compatible with g.

options.text: g starts no later than o, so g comes first in any schedule
options.explanation: Start times aren't what matter; g could start before o and still overlap nothing in O − {o}, but the reason is its early end.

options.text: Since greedy chose g, it must be in every optimal schedule
options.explanation: That's circular, and false: optimal schedules needn't contain g. The argument only shows *some* optimal schedule does.

workedExample:
The structure of an exchange argument:

1. Take an arbitrary optimal solution O.
2. If it already agrees with greedy's first choice, done.
3. Otherwise, modify it to include the greedy choice and show it stays valid and no worse.

Here, O's intervals after o all start at or after o ends (O is valid and o is first), and g ends no later than o because g finishes earliest of *all* intervals:

```formula
e_g ≤ e_o ≤ s_x
O' = O − {o} + {g}
|O'| = |O|
where
e_g: the end time of g (written g.end in the options)
e_o: the end time of o (o.end)
s_x: the start time of any other interval x in O
g: the interval that finishes earliest of all intervals — greedy's first choice
o: the first interval in the optimal schedule O
O: an optimal schedule, a set of intervals
O': the new schedule after the swap
{o}, {g}: the sets containing just o and just g
−: set difference: remove these elements
+: add these elements to the set
|O|: the number of intervals in O
≤: is at or before
In words: every other interval in O starts after g has ended, so swapping o for g keeps the schedule valid and the same size.
```

O' is valid, the same size, and therefore also optimal. Then induct on the subproblem of intervals starting at or after the end of g.
